newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PLAY SUSPENDED IN U.S. OPEN BY LIGHTNING THREAT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PLAY SUSPENDED IN U.S. OPEN BY LIGHTNING THREAT.

text.p: Play was temporarily suspended in the third round of the U.S. Open on Saturday for the second consecutive day due to lightning in the area.
The players were ordered off Congressional Country Club's course at 5:06 p.m. EDT (2106 GMT) when a thunder storm sudddenly hit Congressional Country Club.

Second-round leader Tom Lehman and Jeff Maggert were tied for the lead at five under par when the siren sounded to halt play. Still playing the front nine, they were one stroke ahead of Hal Sutton, who eagled the eighth hole, and young Stewart Cink, who had been one behind when the day started.

First-round leader Colin Monrtgomerie, who recovered from a poor second round, was at two under par at the 12th hole, while Tiger Woods, who struggled on the outgoing nine, was at one over par on the 11th.
The second round was suspended for two hours 18 minutes on Friday due to the dangerous weather conditons.
